texts.facts: 2. Bereft of elaborate details, facts relevant and essential for disposal of the instant criminal revision are that on 10.03.1993, the Food Inspector Shri Inderjeet Rai submitted a complaint [2023:RJ-JD:38888] (2 of 5) [CRLR-1089/2002] against the present petitioner under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. In the complaint, he alleged that on 18.10.1992 at about 7:30 AM when he reached at Sonari Road from Nohar for inspection, the present petitioner was selling buffalo milk. The inspection was done and during inspection, no permission letter was found with the petitioner. On suspicion about the purity of milk, the Food Inspector purchased 750 ML milk from the petitioner and after preparing the sample, Rojnamcha was prepared. The sample was Mohan Lal vs State (2023:Rj-Jd:38888) on 8 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85810569/ 1 sent to health laboratory and on receiving the report, the same was found to be adulterated. Therefore, the complaint was filed in the Court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Nohar and the present petitioner was summoned through bailable warrant. 3. The Learned Magistrate framed charge against the petitioner for the offence under Section 7/16 of PF Act and upon denial of guilt by him, commenced the trial. During the course of trial, the prosecution in order to prove the offence, examined its witnesses. The accused, upon being confronted with the prosecution allegations, in his statement under Section 313 CrPC, denied the allegations and claimed to be innocent. Hence, this revision petition is filed before this court.
texts.arguments: He submits that the incident in the present case pertains to the year 1992. The petitioner was 31 years of age at that time. He was not having any criminal antecedents and it was the first criminal case registered against him. No adverse remark has been passed over his conduct except the impugned judgment. The petitioner has already suffered agony of protracted trial of 30 years. The petitioner has remained in custody for a period of 18 days out of total sentence of six months RI. With these submissions, learned counsel prays that by taking a lenient view, the sentence awarded to the petitioner may be reduced to the period already undergone. Thus, guided by the judicial pronouncements made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the cases of Haripada Das Vs. State of West Bangal, reported in (1998 9 SCC 678 and Alister Anthony Pareira vs. State of Maharashtra reported in 2012 2 SCC 648 and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, age of petitioner, his criminal antecedents, his status in the society and the fact that he faced financial hardship and had to go through mental agony, this court is of the view that ends of justice would be met, if sentence imposed upon the petitioner is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
